newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Wafabank 1996 profits up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Wafabank 1996 profits up 20 pct.

text.p: Morocco's Wafabank, a family-owned bank, said on Friday it made a net profit of 242 million dirhams in calendar 1996, up 20 percent on the 201 million dirhams of the previous year.

A bank official, in a statement sent to Reuters, said deposits totalled 13.8 billion dirhams, an increase of 14.25 percent over the previous period, lifting the bank's market share to 9.8 percent from nine percent.
Loans to clients rose just over 16 percent to 11.1 billion dirhams, while its mutual funds raised 997 million dirhams, 37 percent of the market.

A private Moroccan group owns 50.4 percent of Wafabank. Another 10.4 percent, previously held by French Groupe Suez, was ceded last July to Indosuez Bank group. The remaining 39.2 percent of Wafabank's equity is publicly owned.
The bank said it was paying a dividend of 13 dirhams per share for 1996 against 12 dirhams for 1995.
Wafabank, which is listed on the Casablanca stock exchange, traded at 726 dirhams on March 6.
